prompt: According to the big bang theory, what existed in the universe before the big bang?

### 1. The Classical View (General Relativity)
In the standard model of cosmology based on Albert Einstein’s General Relativity, the Big Bang was not an explosion of matter *into* an empty space, but rather the rapid expansion *of* space and time themselves.

Stephen Hawking famously compared asking "What happened before the Big Bang?" to asking **"What is north of the North Pole?"** Just as there is no land further north than the North Pole because the geometry of the Earth ends there, the classical theory suggests that time is a dimension that started at the singularity. Therefore, there was no "before" because time did not exist yet.

### 2. The Quantum View (Cosmic Inflation)
Many physicists believe the "Big Bang" was actually the end of an even earlier phase called **Cosmic Inflation**. 

In this theory, before the hot, dense state we call the Big Bang, the universe consisted of a "false vacuum" filled with a high-energy field (the inflaton field). This field caused the universe to expand exponentially fast—doubling in size every fraction of a second. When this inflation ended, the energy from that field was dumped into space, transforming into the hot soup of particles and radiation that we identify as the start of the Big Bang.
